findings.title: Missing 'sender' metadata causes KeyError (500) in user validation
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes the Integration already has `sender` metadata. `build_integration` only sets it when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and the webhook that populates it may not have arrived yet. Older integrations also lack it. In those cases this raises KeyError and returns a 500 rather than the friendly error page. Use `.get()` and treat a missing sender as a failure (or a deliberate fallback).

findings.title: No error handling for token exchange and user-info requests
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` and `get_user_info` are called outside the try block. Network errors or a non-JSON response from GitHub raise unhandled exceptions and produce a 500 instead of the error page. Only the body read and parse are wrapped, so the `except Exception` covers just part of the exchange.

findings.title: Unencoded redirect_uri and state in the authorize URL
findings.body: The authorize URL is built by string interpolation, so `redirect_uri` is not URL-encoded. It currently works only because the value is simple. Use `urlencode` to build the query.

findings.title: User validation skipped when the Integration does not yet exist
findings.body: If no Integration exists for the installation_id, the code goes straight to `next_step()` without comparing the authenticated GitHub user to the installer. A first-time install therefore never checks that the OAuth user is the one who installed the app. Anyone who knows an installation_id could claim it before the webhook creates the Integration. The check only applies in the already-existing case.
